PullRequest.Title: agentHost: expose remote Host Settings

## Summary

Host Settings for Mission Control connections displayed `{}` because the relay replaced the host's root configuration with a project catalogue whose schema had no properties.

Expose the complete configuration schema and values to authenticated owner connections and allow explicit Host Settings edits on active connections. This intentionally includes configuration values that may contain credentials. Unauthenticated/unverified connections still cannot read or change host configuration, passive connections remain read-only, and automatic viewer-settings synchronization and remote managed-permission changes remain disabled.

Overlay the listener-owned project catalogue without modifying native host configuration. Preserve it through settings replacement, live updates, and sequence-correct reconnect replay. Exclude listener-owned catalogue fields from incoming edits while retaining native settings in the same namespace. Reject read-only host-property overrides and preserve those values when omitted from a replacement. Update the related contract documentation and regression tests.

## Validation

- `npm run build-fast -- --client-only` — passed after merging current `origin/main`.
- `npm run typecheck-client` — passed.
- `npm run eslint -- src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/protocolServerHandler.ts src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/protocolServerHandler.test.ts` — passed.
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/protocolServerHandler.test.ts --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/electron-browser/agentHostProtocolClient.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/providers/agentHost/test/browser/agentHostSettingsFileSystemProvider.test.ts --grep 'ProtocolServerHandler|authenticates before refreshing its minimal root snapshot|AgentHostSettingsFileSystemProvider' --reporter spec` — 324 passing, 1 pending.

Manual verification: run the updated host, reconnect to a Mission Control session, open Host Settings, confirm the full schema/values appear, save an edit, and reconnect to confirm it persists. The updated remote-host build has not been exercised live as part of this change.

(Written by Copilot)

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The changed allocation, one-second project-progress caller, 1,000-entry replay lifetime, per-client broadcast, and JSON serialization boundary are all directly traced. Exact config sizes and simultaneous lane counts vary, which limits severity but not the mechanism.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Deep-cloned host-configuration objects retained for replay, plus JSON-serialized Web PubSub bytes for each authenticated relay lane
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Cost is O(root-config size) per RootConfigChanged event for cloning/retention and O(root-config size × authenticated root subscribers) for serialization and network. Listener-owned project clone progress emits such an event once per second, and up to 1,000 projected snapshots remain reachable through replay-buffer keys.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Increased CPU/GC pressure, retained memory, and relay bandwidth/queue occupancy; large host settings can delay other Mission Control traffic during long project clones or repeated settings updates.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Listener-owned project updates were replayed and broadcast as their small catalogue action, while native host-config updates were not projected to relay clients, so neither path copied and transmitted the complete host value bag for every update.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Every successful root-config envelope now deep-clones the complete current host values, marks that copy as a replacement action, stores it in the projection WeakMap, and substitutes it during live broadcast and reconnect replay.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT line 3284 introduces `deepClone(this._stateManager.rootState.config?.values ?? {})` inside the per-envelope broadcast/replay path; the same added block replaces the original patch with that complete value bag.
Findings.Title: Keep incremental root updates out of full-config replay snapshots
Findings.Impact: A long repository clone publishes catalogue progress once per second. On hosts with sizable MCP server env/header maps, terminal rule maps, or customization lists, each tick now allocates and retains another full settings copy and sends the whole bag to every authenticated Mission Control window instead of sending only the changed catalogue data.
Findings.Evidence: The added deepClone at line 3284 copies `_stateManager.rootState.config.values` for every successful RootConfigChanged envelope, including listener-owned events. Lines 3287-3289 store that full copy as `replace: true`; `_replayBuffer` holds up to `REPLAY_BUFFER_CAPACITY = 1000` key envelopes, keeping the corresponding WeakMap values alive. `_broadcastAction` projects this envelope separately to each relevant client, and `MissionControlProtocolServer._publish` JSON-stringifies publish frames. `MissionControlProjects._driveClone` invokes `_publish()` through a 1,000 ms ThrottledDelayer, making long clone progress a realistic repeated trigger.
Findings.Recommendation: Preserve patch semantics for non-replacement actions. Merge the listener overlay only into affected overlapping top-level namespaces (for example `copilot`) and retain a full snapshot only for true replacement actions or snapshot fallback, so replay ordering remains correct without copying every unrelated host setting.

Scenarios.Scenario: An authenticated owner opens Host Settings or reconnects after replay is unavailable
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Authentication must complete, then initialize/subscribe/reconnect must project the root snapshot and enqueue its Web PubSub response before the client can render Host Settings.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: JSON-serialize and publish the projected root snapshot over Web PubSub
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One response per initialize/subscribe/reconnect snapshot per lane; chunked above the transport threshold
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Authenticated relay snapshots replaced native host configuration with the much smaller listener-owned project catalogue; the full host schema and values were not transmitted.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The complete response must be enqueued and delivered before Host Settings can render.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One complete root schema/value bag per subscribing lane; size grows with registered configuration schemas, MCP server definitions, terminal rules, and customization entries.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Each lane is handled independently. Snapshot projection deep-clones per request; the relay uses bounded per-client outbound queues and chunking for large payloads.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: There is no projected-snapshot cache. A warm reconnect within the 1,000-action window uses replay; a cold reconnect or replay miss rebuilds and sends a full snapshot.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: snapshot cloning and the JSON/Web PubSub boundary are direct in the traced call path.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Host schema/value size varies substantially, but this is generally one cold-path transfer per lane.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate finding: the one-time full transfer is required by the feature and is bounded by connection/subscription frequency.

Scenarios.Scenario: A Mission Control client clones a repository and observes catalogue progress
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The git clone subprocess drives progress callbacks. A global one-second throttler publishes catalogue state; publication is not on the subprocess completion dependency, but synchronous cloning/projection/serialization runs on the host event loop and each relay update must traverse the outbound queue before progress is visible.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One subprocess per clone request; independent clones may overlap
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same git clone subprocess and one-second progress throttling existed before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The subprocess determines clone completion and emits progress. Its invocation and cardinality are unchanged by this diff.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Deep-clone the full host value bag, retain it as a replacement replay envelope, and JSON-encode the publication
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One full clone per coalesced progress publication and one JSON publication per authenticated root subscriber
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Each listener-owned progress event carried only the catalogue action; it did not snapshot unrelated native host settings.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Consumes host event-loop CPU and outbound queue capacity before each progress update can be delivered.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Publish the full projected replacement through Web PubSub
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once per progress tick per authenticated subscribed lane, with payload size proportional to all host settings
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same publication carried only project catalogue values.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Can occupy bounded relay queues and delay other traffic for the same lanes.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Clone duration controls event count at up to one catalogue publication per second globally. Cost per publication grows with the entire host value bag and authenticated root-subscriber count, not just the changed project progress.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Multiple clone subprocesses can overlap, but the shared ThrottledDelayer coalesces catalogue publications to at most one per second. Each publication fans out to every authenticated subscribed lane; transport queues and in-flight sends are bounded.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No payload cache or delta projection is used. Every tick deep-clones current host values; projected replacements remain reachable while their source envelopes occupy the 1,000-entry replay buffer.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: the one-second caller, full deep clone, replay retention, per-client fan-out, and JSON network boundary are directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Clone durations, host-config sizes, and simultaneous Mission Control windows vary; large MCP/rule/customization maps make the amplification materially larger.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable medium regression: submitted a finding to preserve incremental updates instead of generating full-config replacements.

Scenarios.Scenario: An authenticated active owner explicitly saves Host Settings
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The dispatch is serialized per relay client, strips listener-owned overlay fields, checks read-only properties, dispatches the authoritative action, and emits the echo. Persistence is queued asynchronously and is not required for the immediate protocol acknowledgment.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Receive the settings dispatch and publish the authoritative root-config echo
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One request and one echo per save per relevant subscriber
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Relay root-config edits were rejected and successful host-config echoes were hidden from relay clients.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Dispatch and echo are on the save acknowledgment path; the full projected echo amplification is covered by the submitted finding.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Serialize and write agent-host-config.json through the configuration service
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One queued write per accepted save, serialized globally by `_rootConfigWrite`
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The persistence implementation already existed, but relay clients could not reach it via explicit Host Settings edits.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Queued after dispatch and not awaited by the immediate protocol response; it is required for durable settings.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One incoming value bag per explicit save; validation scales with overlay depth, read-only property count, and edited value size.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Dispatches from the same client are sequenced. Root-config file writes use the existing `_rootConfigWrite` promise chain, so saves persist serially rather than bursting filesystem operations.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache is involved. Current root values and schema are read in memory; replacement writes serialize the current persisted value bag.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: authorization, per-client sequencing, dispatch, broadcast, and queued persistence are directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Explicit saves are user-driven and normally infrequent; configuration size controls validation and write cost.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional finding: the new filesystem write is necessary for the requested edit semantics, low-frequency, and already serialized; repeated full-config echo cost is included in the submitted finding.

Scenarios.Scenario: Native host configuration changes while authenticated Mission Control windows are subscribed
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The native action updates authoritative state, then the protocol handler records replay state and synchronously projects/broadcasts it to relevant lanes. The native producer does not await remote delivery, but relay serialization shares the host event loop.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Serialize and publish a full replacement action for a native root-config patch
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One full payload per native config event per authenticated subscribed lane
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Successful native root-config updates were not sent to relay clients.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the producer's remote-delivery dependency but synchronous projection/serialization consumes event-loop time and queue capacity.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Event count is driven by native root-setting/transient updates; cost now scales with complete host-config size and authenticated subscriber count for every patch.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Each event is processed synchronously by the handler and then fans out across active client records. Per-lane Web PubSub queues bound in-flight work but do not deduplicate identical payloads across lanes.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No coalescing or projected-value cache exists. Each accepted patch makes a fresh full clone and replay snapshot, even when only one root key changed.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the state-manager event subscription routes every RootConfigChanged action through the new full-clone projection.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Native root-setting changes are usually less frequent than clone progress, but transient/config producers and value sizes vary.
Scenarios.Verdict: Covered by the submitted incremental-update finding; no duplicate issue filed.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all five changed files. One medium-confidence-independent, high-mechanism-confidence regression was submitted: incremental root/catalogue updates now allocate, retain, serialize, and fan out complete host-setting snapshots.
